steps.text: Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil, remove from heat, cover, and let eggs stand in hot water for 10 to 12 minutes. Remove eggs from hot water, cool under cold running water, and peel.
Combine mayonnaise, green onions, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, and yellow mustard in a large bowl until well combined.
Chop eggs into big chunks; add to the bowl with dressing. Gently stir until evenly combined; season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Jen's Heavenly Egg Salad
raw_recipe.description: Jen's heavenly egg salad recipe is made with mayo, tangy Dijon mustard, tart yellow mustard, and lemon juice with some green onions for color and crunch.

review.reviewBody: Ok. This is my first review and I've been hesitant to place it because who am I to say...? Anyway, I had to comment on this one. If I'm going to use a recipe, I like to follow it exactly. This endeavor is difficult when the recipe reads, "1/2 lemon, juiced". I juiced half a lemon and, against my better judgement, added the full 3 + tablespoons it yeilded. My dressing was then so watery and SOOO tangy, making a very runny and tart egg salad. I guess I'm still confused why a recipe would call for so much lemon when it already calls for so much (vinegar-based) mayo. That's a lot of acid! I ended up adding 6 MORE eggs. In the extra time I had cooking my second batch of eggs, I ended up adding 3 tablespoons FINELY diced red bell pepper for color and crunch as well as 1 stalk FINELY diced celery stalk, 1 clove of garlic, minced and 1 large basil leaf THINLY sliced. In the end this made a DELICIOUS, not to mention cheap, lunch on whole wheat with baby spinach. Thanks!

Having never used or even heard of lemon juice in egg salad, I was curious enough to give it a try, but not adventurous enough to use the full amount. I probably used half what was called for and it proved to be enough to add a certain freshness but not so much as to be obviously noticeable. I loved the addition of the green onion, and thought the dill and celery I added were nice additions for flavor and crunch. This is a good, reliable egg salad recipe, certainly open to creative touches or additions.

I give it 4 stars because the taste is fabulous! I like to make recipes exactly as written the first time. I thought the juice of half a lemon was a bit much, and it was. It turned out very runny and I found it impossible to make into a sandwich. Next time I will try half a tablespoon of lemon juice.

The flavor is wonderful. I doubled the mustard since I like more mustard flavor in my egg (and potato) salad. I knocked off 1 star because I followed the recommendations to not add all the lemon juice as it may come out too watery. I didn’t and only added enough to make it creamy and didn’t use all the juice. Since lemons come in many different sizes and amount of juice they contain, the directions should specify how much juice to add in teaspoons.

I'm going to rate this recipe because I made it last week using my potato salad recipe. Throw in some ukon golds and dill, cut way back on the lemon juice, and there you have it. It is absolutely delicious. Now, I don't know if this egg salad recipe can replace my go-to, but I do strongly suspect it would taste great. So,enjoy. BTW, for those who don't want so much juice I recommend 2 tsp. Lemon juice and a half tsp. of fresh lemon zest.

It's nice. For all those struggling with the lemon juice debacle. The average lemon produces 1½ to 2tbs of juice if your lemon was larger and produced more then common sense would be just add ½ to 1tbs of juice. Thankyou.
My husband and I loved this recipe. I made the egg salad as written and added some chopped dill pickle. I only added a teaspoon of lemon juice.

It’s a good base recipe. I usually add dill pickle juice instead of Lemon. The lemon added a nice flavor and a change from my normal egg salad. I did use red onion and have tried green onions before but LOVE red onions. I also added chopped celery for added crunch, and I usually add either a small fresh garlic clove or garlic powder. The key difference for me was the addition of lemon. It was a nice change…but will probably keep up with my dill pickle preference…

This is a really good basic egg salad recipe. I just used a splash of bottled lemon juice instead of half a lemon and it was great. Next time I might try adding pickle juice instead and more spices for extra flavor.
I cut back on the lemon juice, added some tiny pieces of dried minced celery, lots of dill, salt and pepper. Extraordinary!

This could possibly be the best egg salad I've ever eaten! I normally only make my egg salad the boring way with just mayo and sugar/vinegar , but I wanted to try something with a little more "oomph" and this was definately it!! I omitted the regular mustard and substituted red onions for the green onions, and added a little pinch of sugar for sweetness. Instead of chopping up the eggs and stirring into the mayo/mustard mix, I used a potato masher to mix it all up together at once, which gives the salad a very creamy consistency.. I will be using this as my go to recipe for egg salad from now on. Thanks Jen!

Good recipe. Here are my swap outs. I used a short 1 teaspoon of bottled lemon juice instead. There is too much give with fresh lemons. Some give more, others less. But if you insist on fresh, squeeze into container, and start with up to teaspoon. To your liking. I omitted salt and pepper, using Lawrys equivalent. I also went with equivalents of Brown Mustard instead of the 2 mustards. Finally, I used Brown Eggs instead. I'm not really a fan of white eggs.

Fun to try! A half lemon was a bit much for me, I put in an extra teaspoon of mayo to reduce the tartness. I like the ideas of bringing in green onion and mixing Dijon mustard with the yellow I usually employ.
I’m not a fan of the lemon. Took a lot of the flavor away
Substituted Boars Head honey mustard for regular yellow mustard and it was delicious.
Very creamy but I used diced jalapeno instead. Gives it an extra kick.
I added some chopped celery and let it sit overnight. It was great. Tye lemon juice really brightened it up.
Tastes good. But gave me terrible heartburn.
